extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and BLM biologists, conservation planners, and stakeholders evaluating Colorado hookless cactus status under the Endangered Species Act
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for evaluating the current and future condition (resiliency, redundancy, representation) of Colorado hookless cactus across defined analytical units (AUs) using the SSA framework, and for assessing threats, conservation measures, and cumulative effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resiliency (AU-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resiliency is described for each AU in terms of habitat and demographic factors needed by the species and calibrated to high, moderate, or low categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a categorical model to identify resource/demographic factors that contribute to resiliency, define threshold values representing high/moderate/low for each factor, score current levels of each factor against thresholds, and average category scores to produce an overall current resiliency score for each AU. Higher resiliency AUs are at less risk from stochastic events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Redundancy refers to having a sufficient number and distribution of sufficiently resilient AUs to withstand catastrophic events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the number and geographic distribution of resilient AUs and whether they provide sufficient redundancy across the species' range to reduce extinction risk from catastrophic events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation means a range of genetic, morphologic, and habitat variation that allows the species to adapt to changing environmental conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether populations across AUs capture genetic, morphological, and habitat diversity (ecological and geographic breadth) needed for adaptive capacity over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stressor assessment using the SSA framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate stressors and other actions that can positively or negatively affect the species at the individual, AU (population), or species levels, either currently or into the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify stressors (current and potential future), determine the spatial/temporal scale of their effects (individual, AU-level, rangewide), quantify current impacts, analyze potential for future increases, and include these analyses in the SSA to determine effects on resiliency, redundancy, and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Livestock use
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess impacts of domestic livestock grazing (trampling, habitat degradation, facilitation of invasive plants) on individual plants and populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate presence and intensity of grazing within AUs, evidence of trampling or population-level effects, effectiveness of BLM grazing management (exclusions, stipulations on permits), and future risk if grazing changes; consider localized vs population-level impacts and include in future-response analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invasive species (weeds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess effects of invasive weeds (e.g., Bromus tectorum, Halogeton glomeratus) that alter habitat, outcompete native perennials, and can expand under drought conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure invasive cover and degree to which invasives are causing localized vs AU-wide impacts, consider interactions with drought and management efficacy, and analyze potential for infestations to expand or treatments to become less effective in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oil and gas development
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess impacts from oil and gas development (surface disturbance, fragmentation, roads, dust, increased access, invasive species introduction) and the spatial distribution of leases/active wells within AUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish leased areas from actual surface disturbance, quantify current active well footprint by AU, account for BLM buffers/no-surface-occupancy stipulations where applied, identify AUs with potential for future increased development, and evaluate likely future effects on individuals and AUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-highway vehicle (OHV) recreational use
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess effects of OHV use (soil compaction, erosion, direct plant damage, dust, spread of invasives), particularly when users travel off designated routes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prevalence and spatial overlap of OHV use with habitat, existing travel management plans and route closures, protections within designated areas (ACECs, NCAs, WSAs, Wilderness), and plausibility of future expansion of OHV routes and associated impacts in specific AUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and maintenance of utility corridors
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess impacts of utility corridor installation and maintenance (plant loss/transplanting, habitat fragmentation, invasive spread), considering that most corridors intersect only small AU portions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document locations and extent of corridors within AUs, account for right-of-way exclusion/avoidance areas in ACECs, consider potential for replacement/expansion of lines or new pipelines in specific AUs, and evaluate current vs potential future scope of effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate change vulnerability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess species' vulnerability to climatic changes (increased temperatures, more frequent/longer droughts) and how climate-driven changes may alter habitat suitability and stressor interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple vulnerability and species distribution models (CCVI, SDMs) and consider differing conclusions; evaluate projected temperature and drought frequency changes under emission scenarios, potential range shifts or expansions, dispersal limitations, pollinator specificity, and interactions with invasive species and management efficacy when assessing future risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical model metrics for AU resiliency
rubrics_metrics.description: The categorical resiliency model for each AU evaluates: (1) habitat condition index, (2) summer water deficit (proxy for drought/soil moisture), (3) survival rates, and (4) minimum population size estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Habitat condition index should incorporate invasive species cover, bare ground, native perennial cover, relative AU size, and probability of occurrence from a habitat suitability model. Define thresholds for each metric representing high/moderate/low conditions, score each AU against those thresholds, and average scores to derive AU resiliency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation efforts and regulatory mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate existing positive conservation measures (BLM ownership/management, RMP stipulations, ACECs/NCAs/WSAs/Wilderness Areas, travel management, species-specific protections, CITES listing) and how they reduce habitat degradation or threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider which measures are binding vs discretionary, their spatial extent within AUs, permanence (e.g., ACECs/NCAs/WSAs/Wilderness Areas are difficult to remove), whether protections are contingent on ESA listing status, and how measures will likely continue or change after delisting; include species-specific RMP stipulations (e.g., 100 m buffers, route density limits, monitoring goals such as 80% populations showing recruitment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of long-term monitoring and population estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use long-term monitoring data and novel sampling-based procedures to estimate survival rates and minimum population sizes for AUs and rangewide assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate BLM and partner monitoring datasets to calculate survival and trend metrics; apply statistically defensible sampling methods (e.g., macroplots and habitat-index-informed sampling) to estimate minimum population sizes and inform AU-level resiliency ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative effects integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate cumulative effects of identified threats and conservation actions using the SSA framework rather than a standalone cumulative-effects analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how multiple stressors and conservation measures together influence habitat condition, survivorship, population size, and water availability, and how combined changes affect resiliency, redundancy, and representation now and under future scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threat inclusion/exclusion rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine which historical or previously-identified threats should be included in the current analysis and which can be excluded based on current evidence (e.g., oil shale development, gold mining, predation, herbicide/pesticide application, collection and commercial trade were determined not threats to existence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base inclusion/exclusion on up-to-date evidence of current and potential impacts to the species' survival or rangewide population trends; explicitly document rationale for excluding previously-cited threats to focus analysis on meaningful factors.
